prompt:
A 3-column by 2-row grid of 6 circular pirate achievement badge emblems, hand-painted game-art style, soft painterly shading and a beveled metal rim. Each badge is a round medallion coin centered in its own cell with generous transparent margin around it. Transparent background. No text, no numbers, no letters anywhere. No glow, no halos, no light rays, no glowing edges, no emissive or luminous effects on anything. Consistent lighting, consistent medallion size across all six. Each badge's metal tier: bronze = humble, silver = accomplished, gold = elite, ornate jeweled gold = legendary. Across this set the relic goes from whole and inert, to cracked, to fully split open, shown through the state of the object itself.

Read left-to-right, top row then bottom row:

Ancient Tackle (silver) — a heavy fishing hook forged from black ancient bone, barbed and pitted with age, resting on dark oiled timber.
Something Old (silver) — a single fossilised tooth-shard the size of a dagger, grey and cracked, seated in a plain brass mount, whole and cold.
Waking It (silver) — the same fossilised tooth-shard in its brass mount, now split by a deep fracture running its whole length, a few chips fallen away.
Fully Attuned (ornate jeweled gold) — the tooth-shard relic fully split open in its mount like a cracked geode, six concentric worked brass rings set around it, the rim heavily jewelled.
Both in Hand (gold) — two ancient relics crossed over one another on a brass rack, one a bone hook, one a tooth-shard, both weathered and pitted.
The Sixth Mount (silver) — a curved section of a ship's gun rail seen from above with six mounting cradles set into it, every cradle filled with a different piece of ancient kit.
